container: Censorship in the arts and media involves the suppression or regulation of content deemed inappropriate or offensive by authorities, institutions, or societal norms. This practice can affect various forms of expression including literature, film, music, and visual arts. While proponents argue that censorship protects societal values and prevents the dissemination of harmful material, critics contend that it infringes on freedom of speech and stifles creativity. History is rife with examples of controversial works being banned or altered, from books like George Orwells 1984 to films facing cuts for explicit scenes. In the digital age, censorship has extended to online platforms where algorithms and policies determine what content remains visible. Balancing the right to free expression with societal protection remains a complex and ongoing debate.
